original_question: Let F = {a1(t), ..., aℓ(t)} be Hardy-field functions of polynomial growth such that every nontrivial linear combination a in span*(F) stays farther than logarithmic scale from every real multiple of every integer polynomial. Must it follow that for every ergodic system (X, B, µ, T) and bounded functions f1, ..., fℓ, the averages (1/N) Σ T^[a1(n)] f1 · ... · T^[aℓ(n)] fℓ converge in L2 to the product of the integrals?
target_in_paper: Section 6.1.2, Problem 23 (Convergence to the product of the integrals)
correct_elements: Your draft captures the core of the paper-faithful problem: the setting of Hardy-field functions of polynomial growth, the hypothesis that every nontrivial linear combination stays logarithmically far from every real multiple of every integer polynomial, the single-transformation averages with integer-part iterates, the ergodic hypothesis, and the desired L2-limit being the product of the integrals.
missing_details: The functions a1(t), ..., aℓ(t) should be stated to belong to a common Hardy field, not just individually to some Hardy field.
The standing notation span*(F) must be made explicit: it is the set of all non-trivial real linear combinations of the functions in F.
The paper’s polynomial-growth hypothesis is part of the standing assumptions in this subsection: each ai has polynomial growth, i.e. ai(t)/t^k -> 0 for some k in N.
The logarithmic separation hypothesis should be written formally as: for every a in span*(F), every c in R, and every p in Z[t], one has |a(t) - c p(t)| / log t -> infinity as t -> infinity.
The bracket notation [ai(n)] should be defined as the integer part (floor) of ai(n).
The dynamical system should be specified as an invertible ergodic measure-preserving system (X, B, μ, T).
The test functions should be specified as bounded measurable functions f1, ..., fℓ in L∞(μ).
The convergence mode should be stated explicitly as convergence in L2(μ) of the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T^[a1(n)]f1 · ... · T^[aℓ(n)]fℓ.
refined_question: Let F = {a1, ..., aℓ} be functions of polynomial growth belonging to the same Hardy field, and let span*(F) denote the set of all non-trivial real linear combinations of a1, ..., aℓ. Assume that every a in span*(F) satisfies |a(t) - c p(t)| / log t -> infinity as t -> infinity for every c in R and every p in Z[t]. Must it then follow that for every invertible ergodic measure-preserving system (X, B, μ, T) and every f1, ..., fℓ in L∞(μ), the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T^[a1(n)]f1 · ... · T^[aℓ(n)]fℓ converge in L2(μ) to (∫ f1 dμ) · ... · (∫ fℓ dμ), where [x] denotes the integer part of x?
justification: This is the Hardy-field 'product of the integrals' problem in the paper, not the neighboring problem on mere L2-convergence and not the recurrence problem. Section 6 introduces the Hardy-field framework, Section 6.1.1 fixes the standing notation for families F of polynomial-growth functions from a common Hardy field and for span*(F), and Section 6.1.2 asks exactly whether the logarithmic separation condition on every element of span*(F) forces the corresponding single-transformation multiple ergodic averages to converge in L2 to the product limit in every ergodic system.
